title: Eighth Word The Unfortunate Brothers Suspicion And Painful State

questions.question: Where did the man end up after traveling over rough land?
questions.answer: He ended up in a lonely, empty wilderness.

questions.question: What dangerous animal came out and chased him?
questions.answer: A lion chased him.

questions.question: What did the man do when he became very afraid?
questions.answer: He jumped into a dry well.

questions.question: How far down did he fall before stopping himself?
questions.answer: He stopped about halfway down.

questions.question: What helped him avoid falling all the way to the bottom?
questions.answer: He grabbed onto a tree growing from the side of the well.

questions.question: What were the two animals doing to the tree?
questions.answer: They were chewing through its two roots.

questions.question: What did the man see at the top of the well?
questions.answer: He saw the lion waiting there.

questions.question: What did he see below him in the well?
questions.answer: He saw a huge dragon near his feet.

questions.question: What else made the well even more frightening?
questions.answer: Poisonous, stinging creatures were all around the walls.

questions.question: What was unusual about the tree in the well?
questions.answer: It had many different kinds of fruit on one tree.

questions.question: Why did the man fail to understand what was happening around him?
questions.answer: He was careless and foolish, so he thought it was all ordinary.

questions.question: What was his inner self doing while his heart and mind were hurting?
questions.answer: His lower self acted like nothing was wrong and distracted him.

questions.question: What did he do with the fruit, and why was that a bad choice?
questions.answer: He started eating it, and that was bad because some of it was harmful.

questions.question: What lesson is given from the sacred saying about how Allah deals with His servants?
questions.answer: A person’s attitude and thoughts matter, and he is treated in a way that matches them.

questions.question: What was the result of the man’s wrong way of thinking?
questions.answer: He stayed in misery, neither escaping it nor finding peace.

questions.question: Why does the passage leave this man and move on?
questions.answer: So the reader can think about the other brother’s condition next.

questions.question: What kind of place did the man reach before the danger began?
questions.answer: He reached a deserted wilderness.

questions.question: What event caused him to run in panic?
questions.answer: A lion came out and was about to attack him.

questions.question: Describe the well he jumped into.
questions.answer: It was dry and very deep.

questions.question: How was the tree inside the well connected to the well itself?
questions.answer: It was growing out of the wall of the well.

questions.question: What colors were the two rats?
questions.answer: One was white and one was black.

questions.question: How does the passage show that danger surrounded him on every side?
questions.answer: There was a lion above, a dragon below, and poisonous creatures around him.

questions.question: What important truth did the man fail to notice about these strange events?
questions.answer: He failed to see that they were not random and that a powerful being was in control.

questions.question: Which parts of him were suffering inside?
questions.answer: His heart, spirit, and mind were suffering.

questions.question: How did his lower self react to that suffering?
questions.answer: It ignored the pain and pretended everything was fine.

questions.question: What mistake did he make with the fruit?
questions.answer: He treated the place like a garden and ate from the tree carelessly.

questions.question: According to the passage, how did he view what he saw?
questions.answer: He took it as normal and as the full reality.

questions.question: What is the final condition of this unhappy man?
questions.answer: He remains in torment without rescue or real life.

questions.question: What happened first that put the man in danger?
questions.answer: He heard a frightening noise and saw a lion coming after him.

questions.question: Why did he jump into the well?
questions.answer: He jumped because he was terrified and trying to escape.

questions.question: What stopped his fall inside the well?
questions.answer: His hands caught hold of a tree.

questions.question: What problem was happening to the roots of the tree?
questions.answer: Two rats were biting through them.

questions.question: What did the man notice when he looked upward?
questions.answer: He saw the lion still waiting above.

questions.question: What did he notice when he looked downward?
questions.answer: He saw a dragon lifting its head toward him.

questions.question: Besides the lion and dragon, what other creatures were there?
questions.answer: There were poisonous stinging creatures on the walls.

questions.question: What made the fig tree different from a normal fig tree?
questions.answer: It carried many kinds of fruit instead of just figs.

questions.question: Did the man understand that these events had a deeper meaning? Explain.
questions.answer: No. He thought they were just ordinary things and missed their hidden meaning.

questions.question: What does the passage say was hidden in these strange things?
questions.answer: It says there were secret meanings in them.

questions.question: Who did the man fail to recognize behind these events?
questions.answer: He failed to recognize a mighty controller behind them.

questions.question: How can we tell that his problem was not only outside him but also inside him?
questions.answer: His heart and spirit were in pain, but his lower self fooled him and blocked that truth.

questions.question: Why was that fruit not safe to eat freely?
questions.answer: Some of it was poisonous and harmful.

questions.question: How does the sacred saying connect to the man’s condition?
questions.answer: It teaches that a servant’s view of Allah affects how he experiences things.

questions.question: What happened because of the man’s foolish thinking?
questions.answer: He stayed trapped in suffering and could not get relief.

questions.question: In what kind of place was the man traveling when the frightening scene happened?
questions.answer: He was in a wild, lonely area.

questions.question: What was the first major threat he faced there?
questions.answer: A lion came out of the forest to attack him.

questions.question: What choice did he make to escape that threat?
questions.answer: He threw himself into a dry well.

questions.question: What object inside the well gave him temporary safety?
questions.answer: A tree growing from the side of the well.

questions.question: What danger threatened that small bit of safety?
questions.answer: Two rats were wearing away the tree’s roots.

questions.question: How did the passage make the dragon sound extra terrifying?
questions.answer: It was huge and lifted its head close to him with a very wide mouth.

questions.question: What do the creatures on the wall add to the picture of the well?
questions.answer: They show that even the sides of the well were dangerous.

questions.question: What surprising sight did the man see near the top of the well?
questions.answer: He saw a fig tree with many different fruits.

questions.question: Why should the man have realized this was no ordinary situation?
questions.answer: The strange mix of dangers and the unusual tree showed that something deeper was going on.

questions.question: What wrong conclusion did he make about all these events?
questions.answer: He decided they were normal and accidental.

questions.question: What was the condition of his heart, spirit, and mind?
questions.answer: They were full of grief and inner pain.

questions.question: How did his lower self trick him?
questions.answer: It made him ignore the warning signs and act as if he was in comfort.

questions.question: What did he do instead of trying to understand his condition?
questions.answer: He started eating fruit from the tree.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention that some fruit was poisonous?
questions.answer: To show that what looked pleasant could actually harm him.

questions.question: What does the passage say about how he is treated because of his understanding?
questions.answer: He is dealt with according to his mistaken view and remains in torment.

questions.question: After crossing rough land, what kind of place did the man come into?
questions.answer: He came into an empty wilderness.

questions.question: What made him rush away in fear?
questions.answer: A lion appeared and was about to attack him.

questions.question: What was the well like that he jumped into?
questions.answer: It was deep and had no water.

questions.question: Where was the tree located that he held onto?
questions.answer: It was growing from the wall of the well.

questions.question: What were the white and black rats doing?
questions.answer: They were gnawing the roots of the tree.

questions.question: What did the man see when he checked above himself?
questions.answer: He saw the lion guarding the top.

questions.question: What did he see below his feet?
questions.answer: He saw a terrible dragon coming close.

questions.question: What danger was spread around the inside walls?
questions.answer: Harmful stinging creatures were gathered there.

questions.question: What made the tree seem very strange?
questions.answer: It had many kinds of fruit from different trees.

questions.question: What important idea did the man miss about all these strange things?
questions.answer: He missed that they were not random and were under powerful control.

questions.question: What was happening inside him even though he acted differently on the outside?
questions.answer: Deep inside, his heart, spirit, and mind were crying out in pain.

questions.question: How did his lower self respond to that pain?
questions.answer: It denied the seriousness of the situation and sought enjoyment.

questions.question: What did he choose to do with the fruit?
questions.answer: He began eating it like someone relaxing in a garden.

questions.question: Why is that action a sign of self-deception?
questions.answer: He acted as if he was safe when he was really in great danger.

questions.question: How does the passage describe his final state before the story moves on?
questions.answer: He is left suffering, with no true relief and no escape.

questions.question: What kind of journey scene opens this part of the story?
questions.answer: It opens with a man wandering through a harsh wilderness.

questions.question: Which animal caused the man’s first shock and fear?
questions.answer: A lion did.

questions.question: What did fear push him to do right away?
questions.answer: It pushed him to jump into a dry well.

questions.question: How did he avoid falling all the way to the bottom?
questions.answer: He caught a tree halfway down.

questions.question: What detail shows that his support would not last forever?
questions.answer: Two rats were chewing through the tree’s roots.

questions.question: What was waiting at the top of the well?
questions.answer: The lion was waiting there.

questions.question: What terrifying creature was below him?
questions.answer: A huge dragon was below him.

questions.question: What smaller dangers were near him too?
questions.answer: Poisonous stinging creatures were around him.

questions.question: What was special about the fruit tree he saw?
questions.answer: One tree carried many different kinds of fruit.

questions.question: What should the man have understood from this strange scene?
questions.answer: He should have understood that it was full of hidden meaning and not mere chance.

questions.question: What did he fail to understand about the one behind these events?
questions.answer: He failed to see that a powerful being was directing them.

questions.question: What does the passage say his heart, spirit, and mind were doing?
questions.answer: They were grieving deeply.

questions.question: What did his lower self do instead of listening to that inner grief?
questions.answer: It ignored the grief and busied itself with pleasure.

questions.question: What poor choice did he make because of this?
questions.answer: He ate fruit carelessly, even though some of it was harmful.

questions.question: What connection is made between a servant’s thoughts and what happens to him?
questions.answer: The passage teaches that a person’s way of thinking shapes how he is dealt with.

questions.question: What overall lesson can we learn from the unhappy man’s story?
questions.answer: Wrong thinking and selfish desire can blind a person to truth and keep him in suffering.
